passages.text: After this, Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews there were trying to kill Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
After these things happened, Jesus traveled in Galilee.
He did not want to travel in Judea.
The Jews in Judea were trying to kill Him.
passages.original: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα περιεπάτει ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ οὐ γὰρ ἤθελεν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περιπατεῖν ὅτι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι

passages.text: However, the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.
passages.sermon: The Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.\r\nThis feast was an important celebration for the Jews.\r\nThe time for this feast was approaching.
passages.original: ἦν δὲ ἐγγὺς ἡ ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἡ σκηνοπηγία

passages.text: So Jesus’ brothers said to Him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had brothers.
His brothers spoke to Him.
They said, “Leave this place.
Go to Judea.
Your disciples are in Judea.
They can see the works you are doing there.”
passages.original: εἶπον οὖν πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Μετάβηθι ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ἵνα καὶ οἱ μαθηταί σου θεωρήσουσιν τὰ ἔργα σοῦ ἃ ποιεῖς

passages.text: For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world.”
passages.sermon:
No one acts in secret if he wants to be known openly.
Anyone who seeks public attention does not hide his actions.
You are doing these works.
Show Yourself to the world.
passages.original: οὐδεὶς γάρ τι ἐν κρυπτῷ ποιεῖ καὶ ζητεῖ αὐτὸς ἐν παρρησίᾳ εἶναι εἰ ταῦτα ποιεῖς φανέρωσον σεαυτὸν τῷ κόσμῳ

passages.text: For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus had brothers.\r\nHis brothers did not believe in Him.
passages.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπίστευον εἰς αὐτόν

passages.text: Therefore Jesus told them, “Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His brothers.
His brothers did not believe in Him.
Jesus said, “My time has not yet come.
Your time is always ready.
You can act at any time.
I must wait for the right time.”
passages.original: Λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὁ καιρὸς ὁ ἐμὸς οὔπω πάρεστιν ὁ δὲ καιρὸς ὁ ὑμέτερος πάντοτέ ἐστιν ἕτοιμος

passages.text: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His brothers.
His brothers did not believe in Him.
Jesus said, “The world cannot hate you.
The world hates Me.
I testify about the world.
I say that the works of the world are evil.”
passages.original: οὐ δύναται ὁ κόσμος μισεῖν ὑμᾶς ἐμὲ δὲ μισεῖ ὅτι ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ πονηρά ἐστιν

passages.text: Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His brothers.
He told them to go up to the feast.
He said, “I am not going up to this feast.
My time has not yet come.”
passages.original: ὑμεῖς ἀνάβητε εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν ἐγὼ οὐκ ἀναβαίνω εἰς τὴν ἑορτὴν ταύτην ὅτι ὁ ἐμὸς καιρὸς οὔπω πεπλήρωται

passages.text: Having said this, Jesus remained in Galilee.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke these words.\r\nHe stayed in Galilee.
passages.original: Ταῦτα δὲ εἰπὼν αὐτὸς ἔμεινεν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ

passages.text: But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, He also went—not publicly, but in secret.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the subject.
Jesus had brothers.
His brothers went up to the feast.
After His brothers went, Jesus also went to the feast.
Jesus did not go publicly.
Jesus went in secret.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἀνέβησαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἑορτήν τότε καὶ αὐτὸς ἀνέβη οὐ φανερῶς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἐν κρυπτῷ

passages.text: So the Jews were looking for Him at the feast and asking, “Where is He?”
passages.sermon: The Jews were at the feast.\r\nThey looked for Jesus.\r\nThey asked, "Where is He?"
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν Ἰουδαῖοι ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἑορτῇ καὶ ἔλεγον Ποῦ ἐστιν ἐκεῖνος

passages.text: Many in the crowds were whispering about Him. Some said, “He is a good man.” But others replied, “No, He deceives the people.”
passages.sermon:
Many people were in the crowd.
They whispered about Jesus.
Some people said, “He is a good man.”
Other people said, “No, He deceives the people.”
passages.original: καὶ γογγυσμὸς περὶ αὐτοῦ ἦν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς ὄχλοις οἱ μὲν ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἀγαθός ἐστιν Ἄλλοι δὲ ἔλεγον Οὔ ἀλλὰ πλανᾷ τὸν ὄχλον

passages.text: Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews.
passages.sermon:
No one spoke openly about Jesus.
People were afraid of the Jewish leaders.
This fear kept them silent.
They did not discuss Jesus in public.
passages.original: Οὐδεὶς μέντοι παρρησίᾳ ἐλάλει περὶ αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸν φόβον τῶν Ἰουδαίων

passages.text: About halfway through the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
passages.sermon:
Jesus attended the feast in Jerusalem.
The feast was halfway finished.
Jesus went up to the temple courts.
He began to teach there.
passages.original: Ἤδη δὲ τῆς ἑορτῆς μεσούσης ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκεν

passages.text: The Jews were amazed and asked, “How did this man attain such learning without having studied?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews saw Jesus.
They knew Jesus had not studied in their schools.
They heard Jesus teach in the temple.
The Jews were amazed.
They asked, “How does this man know so much?”
They said, “He has never been taught by us.”
passages.original: ἐθαύμαζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες Πῶς οὗτος γράμματα οἶδεν μὴ μεμαθηκώς

passages.text: “My teaching is not My own,” Jesus replied. “It comes from Him who sent Me.
passages.sermon: Jesus replied to them.\r\nHe said, “My teaching is not My own.\r\nMy teaching comes from the One who sent Me.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν Ἡ Ἐμὴ διδαχὴ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὴ ἀλλὰ τοῦ πέμψαντός με

passages.text: If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
Jesus had great learning.
The Jews wondered how Jesus learned without formal study.
Jesus said His teaching came from God, not from Himself.
If anyone wants to do God's will, he will know about Jesus' teaching.
He will know if Jesus' teaching is from God.
He will also know if Jesus speaks on His own authority.
passages.original: ἐάν τις θέλῃ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ποιεῖν γνώσεται περὶ τῆς διδαχῆς πότερον ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ἢ ἐγὼ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ λαλῶ

passages.text: He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.
passages.sermon:
A person who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory.
A person who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is different.
This person is true.
There is no falsehood in him.
passages.original: ὁ ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ λαλῶν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἰδίαν ζητεῖ ὁ δὲ ζητῶν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν οὗτος ἀληθής ἐστιν καὶ ἀδικία ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?”
passages.sermon:
Moses gave you the law.
None of you keeps the law.
You are trying to kill Me.
Why are you doing this?
passages.original: Οὐ Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὸν νόμον καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ποιεῖ τὸν νόμον τί με ζητεῖτε ἀποκτεῖναι

passages.text: “You have a demon,” the crowd replied. “Who is trying to kill You?”
passages.sermon: The crowd spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey said, "You have a demon."\r\nThey asked, "Who is trying to kill you?"
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ ὄχλος Δαιμόνιον ἔχεις τίς σε ζητεῖ ἀποκτεῖναι

passages.text: Jesus answered them, “I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He answered them directly.
Jesus said, “I did one miracle.
All of you are amazed by it.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἓν ἔργον ἐποίησα καὶ πάντες θαυμάζετε

passages.text: But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath (not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.)
passages.sermon:
Moses gave you circumcision.
Circumcision did not start with Moses.
Circumcision came from the patriarchs before Moses.
You circumcise a boy on the Sabbath.
You do this because Moses gave you this command.
You do this even on the Sabbath day.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο Μωϋσῆς δέδωκεν ὑμῖν τὴν περιτομήν οὐχ ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ Μωϋσέως ἐστὶν ἀλλ’ ἐκ τῶν πατέρων καὶ ἐν σαββάτῳ περιτέμνετε ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus had healed a man on the Sabbath.
The people became angry with Jesus for this.
Moses gave the law of circumcision to the people.
The people circumcise a boy on the Sabbath to keep the law of Moses.
The people do not break the law when they circumcise on the Sabbath.
Jesus made a whole man well on the Sabbath.
Jesus asked why the people became angry with Him for healing a man on the Sabbath.
Jesus showed that healing a man is greater than circumcising a boy.
Jesus pointed out the inconsistency in their anger.
passages.original: εἰ περιτομὴν λαμβάνει ἄνθρωπος ἐν σαββάτῳ ἵνα μὴ λυθῇ ὁ νόμος Μωϋσέως ἐμοὶ χολᾶτε ὅτι ὅλον ἄνθρωπον ὑγιῆ ἐποίησα ἐν σαββάτῳ

passages.text: Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them how to judge others.
He said, “Do not judge by what you see on the outside.
Judge with right and fair judgment.”
passages.original: μὴ κρίνετε κατ’ ὄψιν ἀλλὰ τὴν δικαίαν κρίσιν κρίνετε

passages.text: Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to say, “Isn’t this the man they are trying to kill?
passages.sermon:
Some people lived in Jerusalem.
These people spoke to each other.
They said, “Isn’t this the man?
This is the man they are trying to kill.”
passages.original: Ἔλεγον οὖν τινες ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμιτῶν Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὃν ζητοῦσιν ἀποκτεῖναι

passages.text: Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood in public.
He spoke openly.
No one stopped Him.
The rulers said nothing to Him.
Some people wondered about this.
They asked if the rulers truly knew who Jesus was.
They asked if the rulers recognized that Jesus is the Christ.
passages.original: καὶ ἴδε παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖ καὶ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγουσιν Μή‿ ποτε ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἄρχοντες ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.”
passages.sermon: Some people in Jerusalem spoke about Jesus.\r\nThey said, “We know where this man is from.\r\nBut when the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ τοῦτον οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν ὁ δὲ Χριστὸς ὅταν ἔρχηται οὐδεὶς γινώσκει πόθεν ἐστίν

passages.text: Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, “You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him, but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching in the temple courts.
He cried out.
He said, “You know Me.
You know where I am from.
I did not come by Myself.
The One who sent Me is true.
You do not know Him.
I know Him.
I am from Him.
He sent Me.”
passages.original: Ἔκραξεν οὖν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λέγων Κἀμὲ οἴδατε καὶ οἴδατε πόθεν εἰμί καὶ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλήλυθα ἀλλ’ ἔστιν ἀληθινὸς ὁ πέμψας με ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε ἐγὼ οἶδα αὐτόν ὅτι παρ’ αὐτοῦ εἰμι κἀκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν

passages.text: So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
passages.sermon: They tried to seize Jesus.\r\nNo one laid a hand on Him.\r\nHis hour had not yet come.
passages.original: Ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πιάσαι καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὴν χεῖρα ὅτι οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Many in the crowd, however, believed in Him and said, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?”
passages.sermon:
Many people stood in the crowd.
Many people believed in Jesus.
These people spoke to each other.
They said, “When the Christ comes, will He do more signs than this man has done?”
passages.original: Ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου δὲ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν καὶ ἔλεγον Ὁ Χριστὸς ὅταν ἔλθῃ μὴ πλείονα σημεῖα ποιήσει ὧν οὗτος ἐποίησεν

passages.text: When the Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about Jesus, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest Him.
passages.sermon: The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering about Jesus.\r\nThe chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers.\r\nThey sent the officers to arrest Jesus.
passages.original: Ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τοῦ ὄχλου γογγύζοντος περὶ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα καὶ ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὑπηρέτας ἵνα πιάσωσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: So Jesus said, “I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nJesus said, “I will be with you for only a short time.\r\nAfter that, I will go to the One who sent Me.”
passages.original: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔτι χρόνον μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι καὶ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με

passages.text: You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, "You will look for Me.
You will not find Me.
Where I am, you cannot come."
passages.original: ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ με καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: At this, the Jews said to one another, “Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him? Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
passages.sermon:
The Jews heard Jesus speak.
The Jews spoke to one another.
They asked a question about Jesus.
They said, “Where does this man plan to go?”
They wondered if they would not be able to find Him.
They asked, “Will He go to the Jews who live among the Greeks?”
They also asked, “Will He teach the Greeks?”
passages.original: Εἶπον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς ἑαυτούς Ποῦ οὗτος μέλλει πορεύεσθαι ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐχ εὑρήσομεν αὐτόν μὴ εἰς τὴν Διασπορὰν τῶν Ἑλλήνων μέλλει πορεύεσθαι καὶ διδάσκειν τοὺς Ἕλληνας

passages.text: What does He mean by saying, ‘You will look for Me, but you will not find Me,’ and, ‘Where I am, you cannot come’?”
passages.sermon:
The Jews heard Jesus speak.
Jesus said, “You will look for Me, but you will not find Me.”
Jesus also said, “Where I am, you cannot come.”
The Jews did not understand His words.
They asked, “What does He mean by saying these things?”
They wanted to know the meaning of His statement.
passages.original: τίς ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὃν εἶπεν Ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ με καὶ Ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν

passages.text: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
He attended the feast in Jerusalem.
The feast had many days.
The last day was the greatest day of the feast.
On that day, Jesus stood up.
He spoke in a loud voice.
He said, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me.
Let him drink.”
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ μεγάλῃ τῆς ἑορτῆς εἱστήκει ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔκραξεν λέγων Ἐάν τις διψᾷ ἐρχέσθω πρός με καὶ πινέτω

passages.text: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus offered a promise to those who believe in Him.
He said, “Whoever believes in Me will receive what Scripture promises.”
Scripture says, “Streams of living water will flow from within that person.”
These streams of living water represent a new, spiritual life.
This life comes from believing in Jesus.
passages.original: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμέ καθὼς εἶπεν ἡ γραφή Ποταμοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ῥεύσουσιν ὕδατος ζῶντος

passages.text: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the Spirit.
The Spirit is the Holy Spirit.
People who believed in Jesus would later receive the Spirit.
At that time, the Spirit had not yet been given.
Jesus had not yet been glorified.
passages.original: τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν περὶ τοῦ Πνεύματος οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύσαντες εἰς αὐτόν οὔπω γὰρ ἦν Πνεῦμα ὅτι Ἰησοῦς οὐδέπω ἐδοξάσθη

passages.text: On hearing these words, some of the people said, “This is truly the Prophet.”
passages.sermon:
A crowd listened to Jesus.
Some people in the crowd heard His words.
These people spoke to each other.
They said, “This man is truly the Prophet.”
passages.original: Ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου οὖν ἀκούσαντες τῶν λόγων τούτων ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ προφήτης

passages.text: Others declared, “This is the Christ.” But still others asked, “How can the Christ come from Galilee?
passages.sermon: Some people said, "This man is the Christ."\r\nOther people asked, "Can the Christ come from Galilee?"
passages.original: Ἄλλοι ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός Οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον Μὴ γὰρ ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ὁ Χριστὸς ἔρχεται

passages.text: Doesn’t the Scripture say that the Christ will come from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived?”
passages.sermon:
The Scripture speaks about the Christ.
The Scripture says the Christ will come from the family of David.
The Scripture says the Christ will come from Bethlehem.
Bethlehem is the village where David lived.
passages.original: οὐχ ἡ γραφὴ εἶπεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ καὶ ἀπὸ Βηθλεὲμ τῆς κώμης ὅπου ἦν Δαυὶδ ἔρχεται ὁ Χριστός

passages.text: So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood among the people.
The people formed a crowd.
The people disagreed about Jesus.
The crowd divided because of Jesus.
passages.original: Σχίσμα οὖν ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὄχλῳ δι’ αὐτόν

passages.text: Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him.
passages.sermon: Some people in the crowd wanted to seize Jesus.\r\nNo one touched Him.\r\nNo one laid a hand on Him.
passages.original: τινὲς δὲ ἤθελον ἐξ αὐτῶν πιάσαι αὐτόν ἀλλ’ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας

passages.text: Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”
passages.sermon: The officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees.\r\nThe chief priests and Pharisees spoke to the officers.\r\nThey asked, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”
passages.original: Ἦλθον οὖν οἱ ὑπηρέται πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ Φαρισαίους καὶ εἶπον αὐτοῖς ἐκεῖνοι Διὰ τί οὐκ ἠγάγετε αὐτόν

passages.text: “Never has anyone spoken like this man!” the officers answered.
passages.sermon:
The officers answered.
No one has ever spoken like this man.
This man speaks in a unique way.
No other person has spoken like him.
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οἱ ὑπηρέται Οὐδέποτε ἐλάλησεν οὕτως ἄνθρωπος ὡς οὗτος λαλεῖ ὁ ἄνθρωπος

passages.text: “Have you also been deceived?” replied the Pharisees.
passages.sermon: The Pharisees spoke to the officers.\r\nThe Pharisees asked a question.\r\nThe Pharisees said, “Have you also been deceived?”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν οὖν αὐτοῖς οἱ Φαρισαῖοι Μὴ καὶ ὑμεῖς πεπλάνησθε

passages.text: “Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him?
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees spoke to the officers.
They asked a question about Jesus.
They said, "Have any of the rulers believed in Him?"
They also said, "Have any of the Pharisees believed in Him?"
The rulers are the Jewish leaders.
The Pharisees are a group of religious leaders.
The Pharisees wanted to show that important leaders did not believe in Jesus.
passages.original: μή τις ἐκ τῶν ἀρχόντων ἐπίστευσεν εἰς αὐτὸν ἢ ἐκ τῶν Φαρισαίων

passages.text: But this crowd that does not know the law, they are under a curse.”
passages.sermon: The Pharisees spoke about the crowd.\r\nThe crowd does not know the law.\r\nThe crowd is under a curse.
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὁ ὄχλος οὗτος ὁ μὴ γινώσκων τὸν νόμον ἐπάρατοί εἰσιν

passages.text: Nicodemus, who had gone to Jesus earlier and who himself was one of them, asked, “Does our law convict a man without first hearing from him to determine what he has done?”
passages.sermon:
Nicodemus was a Pharisee and a member of the Jewish ruling council.
Nicodemus had gone to Jesus earlier.
Nicodemus spoke to the other Pharisees and rulers.
Nicodemus asked a question.
He said, “Does our law judge a man before it hears from him?”
He said, “Does our law judge a man before it knows what he has done?”
passages.original: Λέγει Νικόδημος πρὸς αὐτούς ὁ ἐλθὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν τὸ πρότερον εἷς ὢν ἐξ αὐτῶν Μὴ ὁ νόμος ἡμῶν κρίνει τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐὰν μὴ ἀκούσῃ πρῶτον παρ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ γνῷ τί ποιεῖ

passages.text: “Aren’t you also from Galilee?” they replied. “Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.”
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders replied to Nicodemus.
They said to him, “Are you also from Galilee?”
They told him, “Search and see for yourself.”
They said, “No prophet comes from Galilee.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθησαν καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Μὴ καὶ σὺ ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας εἶ ἐραύνησον καὶ ἴδε ὅτι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας προφήτης οὐκ ἐγείρεται

passages.text: Then each went to his own home.
passages.sermon: Each person left.\r\nEach person went to his own home.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπορεύθησαν ἕκαστος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ
